newsitem.title: GERMANY: BASF says blue pigments escapes, no injuries.
newsitem.headline: BASF says blue pigments escapes, no injuries.

text.p: Nine tonnes of a non-carcinogenic blue pigment escaped from German chemical group BASF AG's main plant on Tuesday, dusting a nearby harbour, after a technical malfunction, the company said.
BASF, one of Germany's so-called three chemical giants along with Hoechst AG and Bayer AG, said some 100 kilogrammes of the material, Heliogen Blue, dusted an area outside the plant's perimeter.
BASF said the material does not cause any sort of itching and is not poisonous. "Indications that the product causes cancer do not exist," the company said in a statement.
A technical malfunction was blamed and no one was injured, BASF said.
